newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian International Olympic Committee official Phil Coles has added his voice to criticism of gender testing of female Olympic athletes. Recently there have been calls to update the chromosome test, in place since 1968, using modern advances in the field of genetics. Page 18

Attacks from within the sport have continued to be launched at the Australian Football League commissioner Graeme Samuel, despite his being returned at the league's annual general meeting last night. In particular the Carlton club has accused Samuel of having conflicts of interests regarding the league's building ventures, for example, the new Docklands Stadium. Page 18

Australian soccer player, Angelo Costanzo from the Adelaide City club, was showered with glass after the team's national soccer league match against South Melbourne in Melbourne. His injuries may result in the loss of his sight. The rioting South Melboune fans have been condemned and the national league is looking at preventive measures. Page 18
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Rugby League will this week consider a proposal whereby clubs if they could not afford to spend at least $A3 million on players salaries, would face either mergers or closures. Under the proposal those unable to pay would not meet the critria for entry into the league. Page 39

Former Australian Wallaby captain Phil Kearns is returning to representative rugby union playing this week after being sidelined for eighteen months with injuries including a sprained Achilles tendon and knee ailments. He will play in the New South WalesA team, in their curtain-raiser match for the Waratah-Western Samoa game on Friday night. Page 40

The merger between the Heidelberg United soccer club and the Collingwood Australian Football League club, has been declared unsuccessful by both parties and will discontinue at the end of the current season. Page 39.
THE AGE

Owners of the Australian race horse Mouawad are hoping to launch him on an international career later this year with his entry into the United States racing in the Breeders Cup Series at Hollywood Park in Los Angels from 9 -11 November. If he does Mouawa will miss the 1997 Melbourne spring carnival. Page C11.

Australian runner Scott Petersen is favourite to win the 1500 metres event at the grand prix meeting to be held this Thursday night in Melbourne. His previous wins include victory over world-ranked Elijah Maru of Kenya over 1500 metres earlier this month and the Victorian 800 metres title. Page C11.

One of Australia's best new bowling talents, Brad Williams has been ordered not to play again this season for fear of aggravating recurring stress fractures on his back. The injuries are so serious that they threaten his long-term career. Williams has so far competed in national competitions and hopes for an international career. Page C10.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Formula One hopeful Stephen White will be returning to Australia in the hope of finding the sponsorship necessary to continue his international career. In Australia he will concentrate on touring car racing . Page 81

Following his failure to win a seat on the Australian Football League Commission, Neil Busse will continue as tribunal chairman. Busse whose election platform opposed the building of the new stadium at Docklands said he was disappointed but not surprised Page 88.

The Australian Football League's revenue for its centenary season last year was a record $A84.84 million. This included an operating surplus of $A38.7 million and a debt reduction of $A3.4 million taking the level of debt down to $A10 million. Page 85.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Rugby League is at odds with its teams over the signing of new loyalty agreements. The ARL wants the clubs to commit to the competition until the year 2000 but the clubs are stalling saying they want more say in the funding arrangements ofthe competition. Page 56.

The New South Wales government has sabotaged the racing industry in that state through extra taxes, according to an influential racing administrator Ralph Lucas. He said that the extra costs meant that the state was no longer competitive with other parts of Australia. Page 51

Australian Davis Cup captain John Newcombe said yesterday that he was upset and bewildered by the angry accusations of Pat Cash, the former Australian world No 4. Cash is angry that he has not been invited to train with the Davis Cup team. Page 55.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
